issues.description: Silent switch from req.stream to req.bounded_stream is unexplained and load-bearing for the new test
issues.detail: examples/things_advanced.py changes body = req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() with no comment, no rationale, and a PR description that misdescribes the change. These streams have different semantics under Content-Length; the new 400 assertion only holds because of this swap. Either the code was bent to the test or a real contract change is undocumented. Name it.

issues.description: PR smuggles unrelated README refactors (handle() signature, status formatting, reflow) under a 'add POST tests' title
issues.detail: The README diff reorders StorageError.handle parameters, swaps str(status)+reason for code_to_http_status, reformats prose, and changes streams — none mentioned in the PR description. Reviewers cannot separate cosmetic from semantic edits. Split into a clean test PR and a separate README/refactor PR with an explicit rationale for the handler signature change.

issues.description: FAQ example fabricates the 400 behavior with contrived handler logic rather than teaching the actual lesson
issues.detail: The stated lesson is overriding headers in simulate_post, but PostTest.on_post layers a Content-Length check, conditional read, and three status codes — with nested if/else and an unbounded read of client-supplied length. The example teaches a wrong mental model and is a copy-paste footgun. Shrink to the minimal handler that demonstrates header override.

issues.description: New POST tests assert status codes without naming the invariant under test
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 check 201 and 400 with no docstring or comment stating the contract (happy-path POST; empty-body-with-nonzero-Content-Length rejected). A future maintainer cannot tell whether 400 is the intended contract or an accident of the bounded_stream swap. Add a one-line spec comment per assertion block.

issues.description: FAQ test uses parenthesized assert — known Python footgun
issues.detail: assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400) reads like a function call and is the pattern that silently passes when given a tuple. FAQ code gets copied verbatim by beginners. Write assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400 instead.

issues.description: Tests duplicate header dicts instead of composing from a shared base
issues.detail: resp3 and resp4 both hardcode Authorization: custom-token and Content-Type: application/json. Extracting a base headers dict and merging the per-case override would make the meaningful difference (Content-Length: 1 with empty body) visible at a glance and shrink future additions.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The PR's headline change (two new POST tests) is reasonable, but it silently swaps req.stream for req.bounded_stream in the example — a load-bearing semantic change that's neither documented nor mentioned in the PR description, and that the new 400 assertion depends on. The README diff additionally smuggles unrelated refactors (handle() signature reorder, status formatting change, reflow) into a 'test PR', making correctness review impossible without splitting. The FAQ example fabricates the behavior it claims to teach with contrived nested control flow and a parenthesized-assert footgun. Split the PR, document the bounded_stream rationale, name the invariant each test enforces, and simplify the FAQ to the smallest example that demonstrates header override.
